newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador declares weather emergency for El Nino.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador declares weather emergency for El Nino.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon declared a national emergency on Thursday to give his government special powers to cope with the El Nino weather pattern, a cyclical warm current that causes rain and flooding havoc in countries on the Pacific ocean.

"Declaring a national emergency helps the government use certain resources. And the economic impact on the country will be great," Alarcon told reporters at the end of a special ministerial meeting in the port city of Guayaquil to discuss the problem.

Meteorological experts have forecast severe flooding and damage to crops in coming months, especially in coastal regions. Heavy rains and flooding already began last week and there were reports of damage to rice, banana and sugar crops, but the worst weather is expected in September.
El Nino last hit Ecuador in 1982-83, causing an estimated $640 million damage.

Public Works Minister Homero Torres said earlier on Friday in Quito that the government had set aside $7.5 million for infrastructure projects to try to soften the impact of the forecast rains and flooding.
"We are preparing for maintenance and repair work on the roads, drains and sewers and to strengthen bridges," he said.
